title: How to add people and company research to an AI agent with MCP
summary: How to add people and company research to an AI agent with MCP: connect Sixtyfour's hosted server and get your fields back with sources and a confidence score.
body_markdown:
It is a server that exposes people and company research as tools an AI assistant can call through the Model Context Protocol. The assistant passes what it knows about a person or company and the fields it wants, and the server returns those fields with the sources they came from. Sixtyfour hosts one at https://mcp.sixtyfour.ai/mcp, with OAuth sign-in or an API key.


Yes. Sixtyfour's intelligence server gives an assistant tools to research one person or company and return the fields you define, search people and companies by structured filters, find or reverse-look-up email addresses and phone numbers, and run Atlas investigations where Atlas is enabled. Each research result carries its source URLs and a confidence score, and anything the research could not establish comes back empty or low-scored for a person to check.


In Claude Code, run claude mcp add with the http transport, the name sixtyfour-intelligence and the URL https://mcp.sixtyfour.ai/mcp, and Claude Code opens a browser sign-in on first use. In Claude Desktop, add a custom connector called Sixtyfour Intelligence with that URL, and Claude Desktop handles the OAuth sign-in when it first connects. Add the docs server at https://docs.sixtyfour.ai/mcp as well, so Claude can look up parameters itself.


Use OAuth where the client supports it, so no key sits in a config file, and otherwise send the key in an x-api-key header. A client that cannot set headers can pass the key on the URL, but Sixtyfour's docs warn that a key in a URL can end up in logs and shared config files. Usage is billed to the organisation of the signed-in user or the key.


Sixtyfour's research tools start a job and return its task ID at once, because a run can take up to ten minutes. The agent polls the job status tool with that ID, every ten seconds or slower, until the job completes, then reads the result and the credits it charged. A start call that times out may still have created the job, so the agent should check its status and never start it again automatically.


MCP tools are charged in credits at the same price as the API endpoints they call. As of November 2026, People Intelligence costs 1 credit a person at the low tier and 20 at medium, Company Intelligence 1 or 5, and polling job status, checking the balance and per-field confidence are free. The Free plan includes 64 credits once.


The MCP server gives an assistant tools it calls directly, with sign-in handled by the client. Agent Skills give a coding assistant instructions and a polling script that teach it to call Sixtyfour's REST API with your API key, which suits an assistant writing code against the API or a client without MCP support. Both reach the same research.
